decisions.reason: As a very close extension of the firm's automation and data-management base, this software benefits from strong absorptive capacity and is more likely to be refined or embedded in broader solutions than withdrawn.

Despite lower past web prominence, it remains closely related to the firm's existing software knowledge, so internal R&D and project learning support retention with only a moderate risk of consolidation.

This safety component fits the firm's infrastructure engineering experience and project business, but because it is less central to the shift toward connected and data-driven offerings its withdrawal risk is somewhat higher.
Control technology for water engineering machinery lies near the core of the firm's machinery, automation, and water-sector capabilities, so management would expect to improve it rather than drop it.

Flow measurement automation and system software aligns strongly with the firm's move toward connected, predictive infrastructure management, and its R&D and research cooperation give it the capacity to continue developing the product.
